# Mohammad Arif

> Product security engineer, security researcher and DEF CON speaker with 5+ years across application security, cloud security, DevSecOps and AI security. This site hosts my security write-ups and study notes.

## Main pages
- [Homepage](https://mohdarif.com/): background, experience, projects, talks and contact
- [All notes and writing](https://mohdarif.com/notes/): index of every write-up

## Featured write-ups
- [JWT Security: Attacks and Server-Side Validation](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/jwt-security.html): How JWT attacks work (alg, kid, jku, jwk, weak secrets, claim and authorization flaws) and how to prevent each one with server-side validation.
- [Kubernetes Series, Part 1: How Kubernetes Works](https://mohdarif.com/notes/kubernetes/k8s-part-1-introduction.html): Part 1 of a Kubernetes security series: cluster architecture, how a request flows, and the core objects, with diagrams.
- [Kubernetes Series, Part 2: Supply Chain Security](https://mohdarif.com/notes/kubernetes/k8s-part-2-supply-chain.html): Part 2 of a Kubernetes security series: check what goes into your images and manifests with Syft, Grype, Trivy, kube-linter and kubesec, and choose a registry safely.
- [Kubernetes Series, Part 3: Monitoring, Logging and Runtime Security](https://mohdarif.com/notes/kubernetes/k8s-part-3-monitoring-runtime.html): Part 3 of a Kubernetes security series: what to log and watch, how to detect attacks inside running containers with Falco, and what to do when a Pod is compromised.
- [OWASP Kubernetes Top 10 (2025): A Practical Guide](https://mohdarif.com/notes/kubernetes/owasp-k8s-top-10.html): The OWASP Kubernetes Top 10 (2025) explained simply: what each risk is, a command to check for it, and how to fix it.
- [Threat Modeling a Multi-Tenant AI Document Platform](https://mohdarif.com/notes/LLM/threat-model-ai-document-platform.html): A worked threat model for a multi-tenant AI document analysis platform on AWS: trust boundaries, attack paths, controls, launch priorities and how to test them.
- [Investigating and Containing Compromised AWS STS Credentials Across Accounts](https://mohdarif.com/notes/aws-security/cross-account-sts-incident-response.html): A worked AWS incident response: trace a bulk S3 download to an STS session using only one account's CloudTrail, then contain it without taking down the services that share the role.
- [SSRF on AWS: From a URL Parameter to Instance Credentials](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/ssrf-aws-metadata-credentials.html): How an image-download feature on EC2 can leak AWS credentials, why three common fixes fail, and what a safe design looks like.
- [Broken Access Control in a Document API: From IDOR to Enterprise Sharing](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/broken-access-control-idor.html): Why a valid JWT is not enough to read a document, why checking the tenant is not enough either, and how to design and test object-level authorization.
- [SQL Injection in Practice: Values, Column Names, Stored Data and Stored Procedures](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/sql-injection-values-identifiers.html): SQL injection beyond the basics: why placeholders work for values but not column names, how second-order injection works, and why stored procedures are not automatically safe.
- [S3 Presigned URLs: Why Revoking Access Doesn't Stop the Download](https://mohdarif.com/notes/aws-security/s3-presigned-url-revocation.html): Why a presigned S3 URL keeps working after you revoke a user's access, how to contain one document right now, and how to design for fast, per-user revocation.
